business_scope.primary_industry_name: Computer Vision Bounding-Box Annotation and RLHF Data Curation

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Quebec (Canada) - Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid - Civil Law (Civil Code of Quebec) for private law, federal Common Law overlay for criminal, tax and regulatory law; French-language statutory regime mandatory for legal publicity and commercial names
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA, in force October 1, 2014)
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)
Canada-China Income Tax Agreement (DTA, 1986, amended by 2009 Protocol)
Hague Convention Abolishing the Requirement of Legalisation for Foreign Public Documents (Apostille Convention; in force for Canada January 11, 2024; in force for China November 7, 2023)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17 (PCMLTFA); Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Suspicious Transaction Reporting Regulations, SOR/2001-317; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, ss 462.31 et seq.; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; United Nations Act, SC 1991, c 45; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky Law), SC 2017, c 21; FINTRAC Guidance 11 (Politically Exposed Persons) and Guidance 12 (Monitoring and Record Keeping). Provincial: Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, and Regulation respecting the legal publicity of enterprises; Civil Code of Quebec, arts 2236-2254 (limited partnership regime); Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Incumbency of foreign corporate general partner (e.g., Chinese or other jurisdiction corporate registry extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry in the foreign partner's home jurisdiction (e.g., in China: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) certified extract; in Canada: Corporations Canada or provincial registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille from the issuer state (China: Chinese MFA or provincial foreign affairs office; Canada: Global Affairs Canada); consular legalization required if issuer state is not an Apostille Convention party

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney (Procuration) appointing the Quebec-resident attorney, agent or registered office representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the country of execution (e.g., PRC notarization office) or Quebec notary / commissioner for oaths
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille of the underlying notarial deed if executed abroad, plus notarized French translation; Quebec-executed deeds require only provincial notarization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified French translation of the foreign general partner's constitutional documents (certificate of incorporation, business licence, articles, UBO declaration)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Certified translator member of the Ordre des traducteurs, terminologues et interpretes agrees du Quebec (OTTIAQ) or court-certified translator
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostilled original source document (Hague Convention) attached to sworn translation; translation itself requires no separate legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Statutory declaration / declaration of ultimate beneficial owner(s) and partners (declaration de beneficiaire effectif) for REQ filing and financial institution KYC
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Quebec notary or commissioner for oaths (Code of Civil Procedure, arts 51-52); notarized and apostilled if executed outside Canada
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille if executed outside Canada; no apostille required if executed before a Quebec notary

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory FINTRAC-compliant domestic and foreign PEP screening per FINTRAC Guidance 11; mandatory screening against UN Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, Global Affairs Canada sanctions schedules under the Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act, Magnitsky List, EU and UK sanctions lists as enhanced cross-reference for dual-listed entities; risk-based enhanced due diligence mandated where PEP, non-resident, or cross-border payment rail (Mass PayPal Payout, Wise) profiles are present; ongoing transaction monitoring per PCMLTFA Suspicious Transaction Reporting Regulations; beneficial ownership verified at a minimum 25% ownership or control threshold and deemed control under FINTRAC guidance.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registre des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) - Registre des entreprises du Quebec (portal: www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11, ss 16, 21 et seq. - the legal name of a Quebec enterprise must be in French; a version in another language (e.g., English or Chinese) may be recognized only as a secondary name where the French version is clearly dominant; non-Latin scripts (Chinese characters) must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet and approved; a Quebec limited partnership must include the statutory French designation 'societe en commandite' or the abbreviation 'S.E.C.'
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Quebec / Montreal (as exclusive geographic markers requiring authorization)
United Nations / Organisation des Nations Unies
words contrary to public order or morality
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the Registraire issues a written notice stating legal grounds; the applicant may immediately resubmit a revised name through the REQ portal with a new availability search; if the revised name is again refused, the applicant may file an administrative review (demande de revision) with the Registraire within 30 days of the refusal notice, under the Act respecting administrative justice, CQLR c J-3, and the rules of the Registraire; a further judicial appeal lies to the Court of Quebec (Civil Division) within 30 days of the administrative review decision; practical remedy is amendment of the proposed name and re-filing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally accepted - REQ requires a real, non-post-office-box physical address in Quebec as the head office (domicile) or establishment of the enterprise; a serviced office or registered agent address providing physical premises, reception and mail forwarding is accepted for registration, but Revenu Quebec, CRA, and banking AML/KYC officers may impose elevated substance scrutiny where the address is purely virtual; a domicile that cannot receive legal process will jeopardize registration and expose the entity to de-registration.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low - approximately 10-15% cumulative probability of a CRA or Revenu Quebec field audit or domicile verification visit within the first 36 months of operation for a non-licensed, low-risk data-labeling BPO; REQ unannounced physical inspections are rare and usually limited to correspondence-based domicile verification, but false or inaccessible registered-office data may trigger summary de-registration.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: REQ name availability search and reservation (attestation de disponibilite du nom)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Estimated statutory tariff per published REQ fee schedule; confirm at filing date

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: REQ initial registration (immatriculation) of the limited partnership (societe en commandite)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Estimated statutory tariff per Regulation respecting the legal publicity of enterprises

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: REQ extra-provincial registration (immatriculation) of the foreign corporate general partner operating in Quebec
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Estimated statutory tariff per Regulation respecting the legal publicity of enterprises

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and Hague Apostille of three foreign partner documents (certificate of good standing, power of attorney, UBO declaration) in country of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign notary / Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs or provincial foreign affairs office (apostille authority)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing consular and notarial market benchmark for three-document bundle

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French translation of foreign documents (OTTIAQ-certified translator, three documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per-page tariff for certified legal translation in Quebec

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial acts and statutory declarations (power of attorney, UBO declarations, partner identification) before a Quebec notary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Quebec notarial tariff and prevailing market rate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office / virtual office (serviced address) first annual fee in Quebec
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Quebec market benchmark for physical registered-office address with mail forwarding

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Professional due diligence, name clearance, AML/KYC file preparation and incorporation agent fees (law firm or corporate services)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Law firm / licensed corporate services provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Quebec market benchmark for limited partnership pre-incorporation and REQ clearance

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, RLRQ c. P-44.1, ss. 2, 19-24, 45-50; Civil Code of Québec, arts. 2236-2250 (société en commandite)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Quebec limited partnership; no escrow account requirement. Contributions are fixed by the limited partnership agreement and may be in cash, property, or services.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the general partner of the Partnership: (1) adopts the Declaration of Registration transmitted to the Registraire des entreprises and accepts the Quebec Enterprise Number; (2) confirms the registered office located at [address], Quebec, and appoints [Name] as the person mandated to receive notices; (3) approves the Limited Partnership Agreement dated [date]; and (4) appoints [Name] as authorized agent to open financial institution accounts, execute government declarations, and supervise AI data-labeling operations. FURTHER RESOLVED, that all officers and agents so appointed are granted full authority to carry out such broader administrative acts as may be necessary to maintain the Partnership in good standing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – online name search and reservation service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the Registraire's online services, validate the proposed French or English name against the Central Register, and file an application for name reservation (réservation de nom) if the name is available. A name that is prohibited, misleading, or identical to an existing enterprise will be refused.
required_dossiers: General partner's full legal name and contact details
Business activity description (ISIC 8220 data labeling services)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, the general partner may submit up to three alternative names or apply for review of the refusal within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary or legal counsel in Quebec (contract governed by the Civil Code of Québec)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the société en commandite agreement in writing, specifying each partner's contribution (cash, services, or property), profit-sharing ratios, management authority of the general partner, and dissolution events. Non-resident partners may sign remotely, but authorization forms are recommended.
required_dossiers: Limited partnership agreement (contrat de société en commandite)
Certified identity documents of each partner
Proof of address and tax identification numbers
If applicable: notarized powers of attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Defects in the agreement can be cured by an amending agreement or a corrective deed signed by all partners.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – online filing portal (Formulaire d'immatriculation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Declaration of Registration electronically, disclosing the general partner's name and domicile, the Partnership's name, the chief establishment address in Quebec, and the business activity codes. After payment of the fee, the Registraire issues the Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) and publishes the filing in the register.
required_dossiers: List of general partners with addresses
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registraire issues a notice of deficiency, the declaration must be corrected and re-filed within the prescribed delay; late regularization may attract administrative cancellation or additional fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate and Annual Declaration Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises / Partnership registered records
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The general partner downloads the Certificate of Registration, verifies all registered data against the agreement, and maintains an internal register containing the NEQ, restrictions on general partners, and the identity of each limited partner. The partnership must thereafter file annual declarations (déclaration annuelle).
required_dossiers: Internal ledger for annual declaration tracking
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any error in the certificate may be corrected by filing a declaration of modification; delays in annual filings can be cured by payment of the late fee and submission through the online portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the enterprise with Revenu Québec for GST/QST accounts and employer payroll deductions if employees are hired; open an employer file with CNESST for workplace insurance; obtain the municipal business permit (permis de commerce) covering office use in the chosen city.
required_dossiers: Payroll and employment information if hiring
Lease agreement or proof of establishment address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late registration with Revenu Québec and the municipality can be regularized through their respective cure procedures; no operating license is required for the AI data-labeling core activity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – no industrial manufacturing permit required; general enterprise registration is administered by the Registraire des entreprises du Québec
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required; if processing personal information, the enterprise must comply with Quebec Law 25 (Act respecting the protection of personal information in the private sector) and designate a privacy officer

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – office-based data labeling BPO does not trigger a full EIA; a registration dossier is required only if backup diesel generators or other listed equipment exceed applicable thresholds
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or VOC emissions; comply with municipal sewer bylaws for sanitary discharge; follow the Quebec Regulation respecting the recovery and reclamation of residual materials for e-waste disposal; maintain non-hazardous waste below 1 ton/month

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification (certificat de sécurité incendie) from the local fire service for commercial occupancy; CNESST workplace safety inspection; structural load inspection for server rooms and cooling equipment; evacuation plan and emergency lighting compliance

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agence du revenu du Québec (ARQ) for provincial taxes and Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for federal taxes, with portals at quebec.ca/revenu and canada.ca/cra
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Register for a Business Number (BN) with CRA at canada.ca/cra-business-number using incorporation documents and ownership details; subsequently register with ARQ for QST if applicable, submitting bank information, tax classification, and partnership agreement
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Limited partnerships are pass-through entities by default under Canadian tax law; no check-the-box election available. Hybrid mismatch elections may apply under specific treaty provisions

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in annual Quebec taxable supplies
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic filing of QST returns through ARQ portal; digital invoicing requirements for large volumes; API connectivity for real-time reporting mandated for certain taxpayers

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and offshore services qualify for 0% QST rate when sold to non-residents outside Canada, requiring proof of export and non-resident status
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Administrative penalties of 50% of unreported tax plus interest; full clawback of zero-rated amounts and potential criminal prosecution for fraudulent zero-rating claims

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada in coordination with the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) for customs currency reporting and FINTRAC for monetary transaction oversight; Quebec-specific foreign exchange business activities are also monitored by the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) for money services business licensing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is a freely floating currency with full convertibility on both current and capital accounts. Profit remittances are unrestricted; there is no exchange control approval, repatriation tax, or prior authorization for dividend or partnership distribution payments to non-residents, provided that transfer pricing and Quebec provincial taxation rules are satisfied. Quebec-specific remittance considerations include withholding tax under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (Canada) and Quebec's taxation act for payments of management fees or interest to non-residents.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory surrender requirements or mandatory conversion ratios. Export proceeds may be held in foreign currencies indefinitely, subject only to Canada's Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act record-keeping requirements for international electronic funds transfers exceeding CAD $10,000. All export documentation must be retained for at least five years under CBSA and FINTRAC rules.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Montreal (BMO) - Quebec Commercial Banking
National Bank of Canada - Corporate Services
Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) - Cross-Border Banking
Bank of Nova Scotia (Scotiabank) - International Banking

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for non-regulatory payment routing via Wise and PayPal Payout, but constrained by Canada's MSB registration requirement under FINTRAC. Offshore EMI providers must be registered as MSBs in Canada if they process CAD-settled payments, or operate through a registered Canadian agent. Quebec requires AMF licensing for certain money services activities. Practical viability rating: High for Wise and PayPal with no direct Canadian bank account, but Legal risk: Medium due to potential unlicensed money transmission if settlement is deemed to occur in Canada.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is permitted by all tier-1 banks if directors complete a video conference interview and provide notarized corporate resolutions. However, several banks require at least one director or senior officer with Canadian residence to attend a physical branch visit for capital escrow accounts. For limited partnerships with no Canadian residents, a sponsored agent relationship with a Quebec-based registered office is mandatory. National Bank of Canada and BMO generally allow 100% remote onboarding for a Low_Risk Standard entity type.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident limited partners without Canadian nexus
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified certificate of limited partnership registration in Quebec (REQ extract), full beneficial ownership schedule (25% threshold), tax identification numbers for each partner, source of funds declaration with audited financial statements, and the partnership agreement showing capital structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border jurisdiction mismatch between wire source jurisdiction and entity tax residency
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Services contract with clearly defined ISIC 8220 deliverables, invoices detailing AI data labeling and RLHF data curation scope, OCED country-by-country report excerpt confirming substance, and payroll/technology asset depreciation ledger proving operational presence in Quebec.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume transactions to mass payment rails (PayPal/Wise) raising money-laundering suspicion
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written AI training data labeling production workflow documentation, monthly reconciliation reports between invoices and completed annotation tasks, client onboarding due diligence files, and FINTRAC-compliant MSB registration certificate if applicable.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing involves direct SWIFT MT103 payment for LP capital contributions from offshore limited partners to a Quebec-domiciled operating bank account, using purpose code 11.4 (Capital transfers under investment) or narrative 'Limited partner capital contribution'. The bank requires a capital account declaration form under Quebec's Business Corporations Act, a capital call notice, and PBS (Pre-Banking Screening) evidence confirming no US tax residency or OFAC sanctions nexus. For transfers exceeding CAD $50,000, support must include a legal opinion on the non-resident limited partner's qualification under the Income Tax Act.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for AI data labeling services are cleared via SWIFT MT103 using standard credit transfer format, with purpose codes 1.9 (Other services: IT services) or 2.7 (Business services). For client fee disbursements, commercial letters of credit are not typical; instead, recurring ACH debits and mass payment via RTP (Real-time Rail) are used. High-value outbound trade payments are settled through CLS-eligible correspondent banking networks via BMO and RBC's USD-CAD dual-currency clearing.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla FX forwards (deliverable) between CAD and USD/EUR, up to 12 months
Cross-currency swaps for USD/EUR cash flows with Canadian chartered bank counterparties
No NDFs are necessary because CAD is freely convertible and full deliverable forward liquidity is available in Quebec
Options (OTC FX options with bank dealer) only for risk management, under AIFMD-like documentation requirements under Quebec derivatives rules

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of the LP's initial registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty assessed under the Act (minimum CAD 34); persistent default after notice may lead to registration cancellation, revocation of legal publicity status, and loss of enforcement rights.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Partnership Information Return (T5013) and T5013 Summary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 following a calendar-year fiscal period; within five months after a non-calendar fiscal period end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 25 per day (minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500); false or incomplete returns may attract additional fines and criminal sanctions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 of the year following the partnership's taxation year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of any related payable plus 1% per month interest; statutory fines for failure to file, and refusal to honor partner deductions until the return is filed.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit threshold for private Quebec LPs solely by size or revenue; mandatory audit arises if the LP is a reporting issuer, or if expressly required by the limited partnership agreement, bank covenants, or an applicable securities law instrument.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: ASPE (CPA Canada Handbook Part II) is the standard Canadian private-enterprise GAAP; IFRS is required for reporting issuers or may be elected by partners; partnership accounting follows the agreed fiscal period.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No separate calendar-year UBO certificate is required for a Quebec LP; beneficial-owner and partner changes are disclosed to REQ within 60 days of the change, with initial disclosure made at registration; any transfer of partnership interests changing registered general partners or material right holders triggers this update.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners (capital contributions and allocation records)
Register of Transfers of Partnership Interests
Minute Book of General Partner and Partner Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $250–$1,000 (typical annual fee for registered office and PQ agent services)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $8,000–$20,000 (if audit required by agreement or lender; otherwise compilation/review fees are lower)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% at the Limited Partnership level because the LP is fiscally transparent; combined general statutory rate for corporate partners: 26.5% (federal 15% + Quebec 11.5%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday applies to an AI data-labeling BPO. Available credits: federal SR&ED investment tax credit (15% general; up to 35% for certain CCPCs) and Quebec SR&ED tax credit (up to 30% refundable for qualified corporations); tax credits are claimed by the partners, not the LP, based on eligible R&D wages and contracts performed in Quebec.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal: T5013 Partnership Information Return (Summary and Supplementary slips); filed electronically via CRA EFILE using a registered transmitter, or via CRA web forms (T5013); requires the LP's 15-character CRA business number.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 5 months after the partnership's fiscal period end (e.g., a December 31, 2025 year-end is due by May 31, 2026); T5013 slips must be furnished to all partners by the same deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the partnership, registered office address, 15-character business number, and fiscal period end date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Canadian address of the general partner (GP); identify the jurisdiction where the LP is formed and list any non-resident partner on Schedule 8.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total taxable income of the partnership computed under Part I of the Income Tax Act before allocation to partners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The portion deriving from a fixed establishment in Quebec is Canadian-source income; separate income not taxable in Canada under section 115.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partner names, 15-character BN or SIN, addresses, province/territory, and country of tax residence; profit/loss sharing ratios.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For each foreign partner, complete the country code, residence status, and attach the T5013 slip; verify the partner is not claiming treaty benefits without a valid TRC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of income, losses, CCA, and other deductions to each partner in accordance with the partnership agreement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Respect the at-risk and limited partner loss restriction rules; losses allocated to a non-resident limited partner are deductible only to the extent of the partner's Canadian-source at-risk amount.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: ITA s. 235 penalty of C$25 per day, minimum C$100, maximum C$2,500; each late or incorrect T5013 slip: C$100 per slip; intentional omissions can trigger criminal prosecution under s. 239 with fines up to 200% of tax avoided and imprisonment up to 5 years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Quebec: Releve 31 (RL-31) - Statement of Partnership Income; filed electronically through Revenu Quebec's secure CLICS portal or an approved EDI transmitter; requires the 12-digit NEQ (Quebec enterprise number).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 5 months after the partnership's fiscal period end; RL-31 slips must be provided to each partner and filed with Revenu Quebec by the same statutory deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name of the partnership, NEQ, principal establishment address in Quebec, and fiscal year end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate the province/country of residence of each partner; the GP's Quebec address serves as the service address.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 1 - Total Income of the Partnership
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec-source income of the partnership before allocation, determined under the Taxation Act.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include revenues from data-labeling work performed in Quebec; do not include amounts attributable to foreign sites or subcontracted offshore labor.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Portion of the partnership's Quebec-source income allocated to each partner for the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident partners, this amount establishes Quebec taxing jurisdiction; the partner must file a Quebec return or obtain a waiver; Revenu Quebec applies the treaty rate reduction only with a valid TRC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partner legal name, country of tax residence, tax identification number, and TRC reference number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory for every direct non-resident holder; omission triggers administrative penalties and reassessment of the partnership.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Revenu Quebec imposes daily late filing penalties (minimum C$50, up to C$5,000 for partnership declarations and up to C$2,500 for slip omissions); deliberate failure to file can lead to reassessment at a 50% gross negligence penalty plus interest and penal prosecution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Federal Part XIII: 25%; Quebec concurrent non-resident levy: 15%; combined statutory exposure for dividends arising in Quebec: 40% before treaty relief.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced withholding, the beneficial owner must deliver CRA Form NR302 (annual claim) or NR303 (one-time claim) before payment, together with a valid Certificate of Residency (TRC) from the home jurisdiction; Revenu Quebec accepts the federal TRC and applies treaty reductions to Quebec's 15% levy; the LP must retain the certification on file. Partnership-specific note: profit allocations distributed to non-resident partners are not Part XIII 'dividends' and are taxed as Canadian business income under Part I; however, interest, royalties, or rents paid by the LP to a non-resident are subject to withholding at the rates above unless treaty relief is certified.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory combined 40% (25% federal + 15% Quebec), treaty-reduced to 10% under the Canada-US and Canada-UK conventions; certain software license payments may qualify for 0% under the US treaty if characterized as copyright royalties for off-the-shelf software. Interest: statutory combined 40%; domestic exemption applies under ss. 212(1)(b) and 212(3)(a) for most arm's-length interest not based on profit participation or revenues; treaty floor for participating debt interest: 15% (US), 15% (UK).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: C$1,000,000 for a single specified transaction, or C$50,000,000 aggregate of all specified transactions with non-arm's-length non-residents in the fiscal year (ITA s. 247(10); Quebec Taxation Act s. 42.0.1 mirrors the threshold below), after which contemporaneous documentation is mandatory to avoid penalty exposure.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada and Quebec do not operate a formal Economic Substance Registration (ESR) regime; substance is enforced through the GAAR (ITA s. 245 and the Quebec GAAR under the Taxation Act), sham doctrine, and the 'full business purpose' jurisprudence. An AI data-labeling LP must demonstrate real Quebec presence: operational management, payroll, decision-making, and physical premises; a conduit LP with no genuine business purpose may be disregarded, causing reattribution of income to the partner and a 25% GAAR penalty.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omitting revenue from AI labeling contracts, issuing off-book invoices, falsifying expense records for offshore subcontractors, or deliberately failing to allocate profits to partners to reduce Canadian tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: On indictment under ITA s. 239: fine of 100%-200% of the tax sought to be evaded plus imprisonment up to 5 years; summary conviction: fine of 50%-100% plus up to 2 years; civil gross-negligence penalty of 50% plus interest on unpaid taxes; Quebec imposes similar penal fines under the Taxation Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the corporate GP are jointly and severally liable under s. 227.1 for unremitted source deductions and under s. 160 for non-arm's-length transfers; CRA may order passport seizure and travel bans under s. 240 where unpaid assessed liabilities exceed C$25,000; criminal exposure up to 5 years imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing and Documentation Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting the data-labeling service fee to a foreign related party without a CUP or TNMM comparability analysis; allocating GPU/cloud costs artificially; failing to prepare and retain a contemporaneous Local File when cross-border specified transactions exceed C$1 million or C$50 million aggregate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ITA s. 247(3) transfer pricing adjustment to arm's-length value; ITA s. 247(8) penalty of 10% of the net adjustment without a floor and regardless of intent; parallel 10% penalty under Quebec Taxation Act s. 42.0.2; interest accrues from the original due date.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve knowingly false TP documentation are exposed to gross-negligence penalties and potential criminal prosecution; CRA may pierce the corporate GP to collect penalties when the LP is used purely as an invoicing shell; in practice, the CRA will assess the LP, then the GP as a jointly liable partner.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Forming a Quebec LP with no staff, no premises, and no business supervision solely to flow funds to non-resident partners; failing to file T5013/RL-31; claiming treaty benefits without actual tax residence; mischaracterizing labor income as partnership distributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR denial of the entire tax benefit plus a 25% penalty on the benefit amount (ITA s. 245; Quebec Taxation Act GAAR); false declaration penalties up to C$100,000 for serious prosecutable filings; reassessment against the general partner personally for the full tax amount where the LP is non-recognized.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under Civil Code of Quebec art. 2244, any limited partner who participates in management loses limited liability and becomes jointly liable for partnership obligations; directors of the corporate GP face joint and several unlimited exposure for the reassessed tax, penalties, and interest; travel bans may be imposed during collection enforcement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / FINTRAC Non-Compliance in Payment Rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating unregistered money service business elements within the Mass PayPal/Wise payout infrastructure; transferring funds in fiat or cryptocurrency without an AML compliance program; failing to report large virtual currency or cash transactions over C$10,000 to FINTRAC; failing to maintain a beneficial ownership register for the LP.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under PCMLTFA s. 73.21, administrative monetary penalties up to C$250,000 for individuals and C$500,000 for entities per violation; FINTRAC may issue public compliance notices; intentional breaches attract criminal prosecution with fines and imprisonment up to 5 years; Quebec's enterprise registry imposes separate administrative penalties for missing beneficial ownership declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and AML compliance officers who 'directed, consented, or acquiesced' in the conduct are personally liable and can be convicted under PCMLTFA; enforcement measures include asset freezes and, where a significant tax debt coexists, Canadian passport suspension and travel bans under collection statutes.
